_meta.locales: Every translatable value is an object keyed by locale. A locale is NEVER mandatory: getTrad (src/js/modules/utils.js) tries the country key (fr-ca), then the language (fr), then any key starting with it, then en-us, then en — so a market with no copy of its own renders English rather than nothing. Adding a language means adding its key next to en-us; nothing else changes. The one rule is never to leave a key as an empty string: the country key is matched before the fallback runs, so an empty fr-ca renders blank instead of falling through to fr. A locale with no copy yet simply has no key. The keys present here also ARE the locale list the dev prompt offers (tasks/prompt.task.js > localesForVariant).
_meta.localeList: Eight locales: en-us, en, fr, fr-ca, es, es-mx, de, nl — the same set SGH ships in 4-card-section-module for this campaign.
_meta.translationStatus: Copy transcribed from the per-locale Figma frames (file qP9YNquHyjNhP5S34X0JRJ). Comparator: en 1093:44584, nl 1249:33206, de 1249:68526, es 1249:59696, fr 1249:77356, fr-ca 1249:42036. en-us is the original desktop frame 1020:42173. The intro title and subtitle that used to live here were REMOVED: the editor authors them in CoreMedia as rows above the module. Their per-locale frames, should they ever be needed again, were en 1093:44580, nl 1249:27015, de 1249:62482, es 1249:53652, fr 1249:71312, fr-ca 1249:35992. es-mx has NO frame of its own and reuses the es copy, as requested. Brand and feature names (Ray-Ban Meta, Meta AI, Transitions®, Bluetooth, WiFi, the app names) are left untranslated exactly as the frames have them.
_meta.source: Copy transcribed from Figma "SGH - RB META APEROL": the en-us reference is desktop 1020:42173, with mobile 1020:47170. Frame 1020:36519 was the section title, which the module no longer renders. The hideWhenOnlyDifferences flags are that desktop frame’s "Don’t show in differences" annotations, on the Meta AI, Lenses, Connectivity, Water resistance and Compatible apps rows.
_meta.productCodes: `upc` is the ONLY product field authored here: everything else about the product — name fallback, packshot, price and the PDP link — comes back from the product service keyed by that UPC. productId (the catentryId) and pdpUrl used to sit beside it as cross-references and were REMOVED: the catentryId is echoed by the response anyway, and a hand-written PDP url can only go stale, because the canonical slug is /{market}/{brand}/{model}-{upc} and the model is not derivable from the UPC — so the link is the storefront's pdpURL or nothing. The authored UPCs are Gen 3 8056266261459 and Gen 2 8056262721339, replacing the Gen 1 Wayfarer / Headliner placeholders (8056597988377 / 8056597988391) the module launched with. WARNING, verified 2026-09-21 against production: the Gen 2 UPC resolves on /us, /ca-en, /uk, /au, /de, /fr and /es (0RW4012, "Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 2) Wayfarer", isOutOfStock) but NOT on /mx or /nl, and the Gen 3 UPC resolves on NO market at all, because that product has not gone live yet — the UPC is correct, so nothing is to be authored or chased: the catalog answers at launch and the column completes itself, and until then it renders its copy with no packshot, price or link. `upc` is keyed by locale: add a key per market that sells a different article, and a market with none falls back to en-us through getTrad. See README, “It takes a UPC, not a product id”.
_meta.icons: Icon values are resolved against package.json > projectConfigurations.paths.productionImage (https://media.sunglasshut.com/table-comparison-component/img/ in production, ./static/images/ in dev), so the brand subfolder is part of the value. An absolute http(s) url is used as-is instead — see isSelfContainedUrl in src/js/contents.js.
_meta.notFromFigma: ONE key has no source frame: comparison.selectLabel, the label above the mobile product picker. The per-locale frames cover the comparator table, which does not contain that control. Its non-English values are provisional. Same for products[].family and products[].shortName, which only feed that dropdown, and for products[].nameBadge, whose English reads "New" in the LC frame and whose seven translations are provisional.
_meta.nameBadge: products[].nameBadge is the pill beside the product name, and it is OPTIONAL. Populated it renders, omitted it emits no markup at all — so it is the switch as well as the text, and the text is free: the frame says "New" but nothing in the code does. It is a locale map like every other authored string, which makes it per market: drop the whole key and no market shows it, author an empty string for one locale and only that market goes without, because getTrad matches a key before it falls back. Never author null. It is NOT the same thing as products[].badge, which is the "Camera + Audio" line under the name and carries an icon; the two are independent and can both be on. The text is authored in natural case, because .ct_comparison__name-badge applies text-transform: uppercase.
_meta.figmaDeviations: Deliberate deviations from the frames, each a slip rather than a choice. (1) es, Gen 3 case: the frame read "Hasta 5 horas de uso con una sola carga" where every other locale, and the Gen 2 column beside it at 8, say 9. Set to 9. (2) es, lens type: the frame read "Dom" for "Sun" — corrected to "Sol". The same line reads "Lunettes de soleil" in fr and "Sonnenbrillen" in de, which name the product rather than the lens type; those are KEPT, as decided. (3) nl and de camera, Gen 3: the frames had an unbalanced bracket, "(t.o.v. (Gen 2)" and "(im Vergleich zu (Gen 2)" — closed to a single pair. (4) es, Gen 2 product name: the frame read "Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 2)" where every other locale reads "Ray-Ban | Meta Gen 2" — normalised. (5) fr-ca, Gen 3 Meta AI: "TRADUCTION EN DIRECT" was the only all-caps line in the table — set to sentence case. (6) Straight apostrophes in the fr, fr-ca and nl frames were normalised to the typographic apostrophe used everywhere else; nl "videos" to "video’s". (7) Unit notation was made consistent inside each locale, because aligning the columns exposed it: fr and es wrote "à 120 fps" on one line and "30fps" on the next, fr-ca spelled out "images par seconde" then wrote "30fps", and fr-ca wrote "1000+ photos" above "Plus de 100 vidéos". (8) fr-ca, Gen 2 audio: the frame spelled the number out, “Ensemble de cinq micros”, where the source has “5-mic array” and the Gen 3 column of the same locale already wrote “Ensemble de 6 micros” — set to “5”. Row labels are stored in natural case because .ct_comparison__label applies text-transform: uppercase.
_meta.colorCount: products[].meta ("3 Colors") is AUTHORED, not live, and always will be. SGH’s documented product service returns frameColor / lensColor / localizedColorLabel for the single variant it describes and no count of the siblings. A count exists in the group’s services — `availableColors` on glasses.com’s /ajaxSearchDisplayView — but there is no SGH equivalent: the two candidate paths answer with the homepage html, not json. Unlike the packshot, the price and the PDP link, which do come from the call.
_meta.columnConsistency: The two product columns are kept in step: any line that reads the same for Gen 3 and Gen 2 in en-us reads the same in every other locale too. The per-locale frames did not do this — they drifted on 29 lines (nl "ultragroothoek" vs "ultra-wide", de "automatische Aufnahme" vs "Autoaufnahme", es "en tiempo real" vs "en directo", and so on) — and the two columns sit side by side, so the drift was visible. Genuine differences (6-mic vs 5-mic, 9 vs 8 hours, 50 vs 48, "flash storage", the extra 36% line) are untouched. If a line is edited in one column, edit it in the other.
_meta.valuesMatchSource: VERIFIED against the original desktop frame 1020:42173. en-us is identical to it line for line, row labels and annotations included. Every other locale carries the same figures: 497 lines compared across the seven translated locales by extracting each line’s numeric values (normalising the decimal comma and the thousands separator, so 5,5 = 5.5 and 1 000 = 1000) and matching them against the en-us line at the same index — zero discrepancies. The structural differences are the same everywhere too: a line the source keeps distinct between Gen 3 and Gen 2 is distinct in every locale, and a line it keeps identical is identical in every locale. Re-run that check after any copy edit — a translated figure that drifts from the source is the one error this table cannot afford.
_meta.perMarketProducts: products[].upc is keyed by locale and resolved by getTrad — exact country, then language, then any key starting with it, then en-us, then en — so a market that sells a different article gets its own key and a market with none shows the English product. A plain string still works and means one article everywhere. comparison.api.store is the deliberate opposite: it never falls back, because the store decides currency, price and discount, and quoting another market’s currency is worse than quoting nothing.
_meta.discountBadge: prices.saleBadgeValue and prices.saleBadgeColor arrive ONLY on a product that is actually on sale, which is why an earlier version of this module recorded that the endpoint had no badge — it was pointed at two full-price products. The string is rendered verbatim and never recomputed from the two figures: the same Tiffany reads “30% off” on /us and “-30%” on /ca-en. The colours are applied inline so the badge matches the promotion running elsewhere on the page. The badge is NOT in the Figma frame, which shows only the offer and the struck list price — it was added on request.

api._devOrigin: Development only, ignored in a production build: the storefront the CORS proxy (npm run proxy) is pointed at, so a live call from localhost reaches real data — and so a dev build can be aimed at stage rather than production. NOTE: on localhost there is no storefront, so window.storeId and window.langId do not exist and NO product call is made at all — the table renders its authored copy without packshot, price or CTA. To exercise the live path from localhost, set both by hand in the console (window.storeId = '14351'; window.langId = '-3') and reload the module; everything downstream, proxy included, works unchanged.
api._upcMissing: The store comes from the page, so every market makes a call — but not every market carries every article. The endpoint simply omits a UPC it does not know, so that column keeps its authored copy, loses packshot, price and link, and logs a warning. Re-verified 2026-09-21 on production with the real UPCs, across nine stores: the Gen 2 (8056262721339) answers on /us 10152, /ca-en 10154, /uk 11352, /au 11351, /de 14351, /fr 13801 and /es 13251, and is absent from /mx 16001 and /nl 19001 — the same two markets that were missing the Gen 1 placeholders. The Gen 3 (8056266261459) is absent from ALL NINE. Fixing a gap is authoring, not code: give products[].upc a key for those markets with the article they actually sell.
api._upc: products[].upc may be a plain string — one article in every market — or an object keyed by locale. The object is resolved by getTrad, exactly like the copy: exact country, then language, then any key starting with it, then en-us, then en. So a market with no key of its own shows the English article rather than an empty column. This is the opposite of the store rule above, and on purpose: an empty column is worse than a neighbouring market's product, while a wrong store is worse than no store.
